step6.stdout:
kith-group — the owner's commands for bot guests in rooms, over the host's local API.

  kith group add-bot <room> <bot> [--json]      let one of your bot guests (Grok) see a group room from now on
  kith group remove-bot <room> <bot> [--json]   take it out of the room
  kith group secret <room> --to <member|bot> [--label L] [--ttl MIN] [--json]
                                                hand ONE member of the room a one-time secret. The value is read from stdin
                                                only (never an argument): pipe it in, or type it at the no-echo prompt.
                                                It lapses in MIN minutes (default 10, 1..60) and can be taken once.
  kith group secrets <room> [--json]            the open ones: id, to, label, when it lapses (never a value)
  kith group secret <room> --withdraw <id>      take one back before it is used
  kith bot ls [--json]                          the bot guests: id, name, state, whose, agents
  kith bot invite <name> [--agent A ...] [--bot-id ID] [--provider P] [--json]
                                                a link for a bot to join (a new bot, or --bot-id: a fresh link for one of
                                                yours); the link is the only token-bearing output, for your terminal only
  kith bot revoke-invite <inviteId> [--json]    take back an unused bot invite
  kith bot revoke <bot> [--json]                remove a bot guest (twice: fine, changed false)
  kith bot decide <bot> allow|deny [--always] [--json]   answer a bot waiting at the door (--always: allow every bot of its owner)
  kith bot auto-allow <person> on|off [--json]  let that invited person's bots in without asking
  kith bot set <bot> [--wake-profile P] [--turn-timeout S] [--json]
                                                a bot guest's wake settings: P is a kith-auth profile of the `grok`
                                                service (what `kith send-to grok --profile P` uses; '' clears it); S is how
                                                long one of its turns may run (the host clamps it to 30..3600)

<room> and <bot> are an id or a name (case-insensitive, exact). Edits are read-modify-write of the member list, so two
edits at the same moment: the last one wins. The host decides who may join (your own active bots only) and says why not.
Exit: 0 done, 1 refused or host unreachable, 2 usage / unknown or ambiguous name.
